candidates.title: sync_stored reports success after an earlier sync of the same directory failed and the kernel dropped the data: a directory that then meets O2's definition reloads with a cached root hash that does not match its contents (or with lost contents)
candidates.component: Emulator core: machine::sync_stored (src/machine.cpp 712-721), os::sync_file / sync_fd (src/os-filesystem.cpp 628-644, 726-769), os::mapped_memory destructor (src/os-mapped-memory.cpp 538-552); contract in src/cm.h (cm_sync_stored: 'On success, all previous changes to the stored machine files are durable on disk')
candidates.role: Honest operator (storing, loading, cloning and syncing machines)
candidates.location: src/machine.cpp machine::sync_stored 712-721 and for_each_stored_filename 617-651; src/os-filesystem.cpp sync_file 726-769 (opens a new descriptor per call, fsync, close; no state kept), sync_fd 628-644; src/os-mapped-memory.cpp ~mapped_memory 538-552 (msync(MS_ASYNC) and close() results ignored, descriptors that were open during the writes are closed before any fsync); src/cm.h 644-653; doc/README.md 5506-5514
candidates.description: A machine loaded with shared backing stores writes through MAP_SHARED mappings; destroying it only unmaps and closes (errors ignored). Durability, and with it the O2 guarantee, comes only from sync_stored, which reopens every file and calls fsync. sync_stored is stateless: when a writeback error happens (ENOSPC or EIO from the storage under the filesystem), Linux reports it to one fsync, marks the affected pages clean and does not write them again. sync_stored throws at the first failing file and leaves no record. Any later sync_stored of the same directory (a retry by the caller, a relaunch by a supervisor, the sync of the next commit) finds nothing dirty and returns success, although the pages whose writeback failed never reached the disk. cm.h promises for that success that 'all previous changes to the stored machine files are durable on disk'. The directory now satisfies O2's definition (machine destroyed without a crash, directory synced after the last change), but after the page cache is dropped (reboot, remount, memory pressure) it holds either stale data pages or, as in the experiment, stale cached hash-tree pages with the dirty-page tree saying clean. A load without a rebuild (the operator's own directory, so O1 asks for none) then returns a root hash that is not the root of the contents. Nothing in the manual or cm.h says that a directory whose sync failed must be discarded. A fix exists inside the emulator (for example invalidating the directory when a sync fails, or keeping the failure sticky), so the false guarantee is the emulator's, not only the host's.
candidates.trigger: No adversary is needed: a host fault that the threat model names (a full disk; here the storage under the filesystem is full or returns an I/O error at writeback, as with thin-provisioned or sparse virtual disks, LVM thin pools, loop images, network block devices, NFS) while a machine uses a stored directory with sharing, followed by the honest operator's own second sync_stored on that directory after the fault is cleared. The guest only decides which pages are dirty.
candidates.reachability: Honest operator's path (storing and syncing; restarting after a stop). The first failure is loud and stops the operator, which section 4 allows. The defect is the second call. It is reached by any caller that retries sync_stored or keeps using the directory after the failure. By reading (not run), the shipped stored player does this on relaunch: prt.lua revert_interrupted_input (2864-2880) keeps the epoch machine directory when a content rehash matches state.json (the page cache still holds the data), and the next commit's sync_stored succeeds. The cartesi-machine CLI user who frees space and reruns --load=<dir>,sharing:all,sync gets the same success. Filesystem behaviour matters: XFS (the reflink filesystem stored machines are documented for) drops the pages and stays writable; ext4 in ordered mode aborted its journal on the failed write to newly allocated blocks in the same experiment (the second sync then fails loudly with EROFS); failed overwrites of already allocated blocks are not expected to abort it (not tested).
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: the list excludes 'Host faults, such as a full disk, as long as the emulator does not turn them into a wrong hash, a wrong proof, or a directory that O2 guarantees but that later loads as a different state (section 4)'. Here the fault ends in exactly that: O2 says 'The emulator guarantees a stored directory only when it was synced after the last change to its contents and, if a machine used it with shared backing storage, that machine was destroyed without a crash before that sync', the second sync_stored succeeds, and the directory reloads with a wrong root hash. So the exclusion does not apply. Alternative reading: a second sync after a failed one is the operator not discarding a directory it should distrust, which would make it Out of scope or Low ('a failure that needs misuse of an API by its trusted caller'); but neither O2, cm.h nor the manual tells the caller to discard after a failed sync, and cm.h promises durability on success.
2 Role: sync_stored and the mapped backing stores are 'storing, loading, cloning and syncing machines (within the limits of O1 and O2)', the Honest operator role of the AUDIT.md table.

3 High and Medium cases: none fits. The Medium case 'A persistence operation that fails loudly, without a wrong hash or damage to a directory that O2 guarantees' does not apply, because the second call does not fail and the result is a wrong hash.

4 Critical: section 4, 'A host fault, such as a full disk or an output channel that refuses a write, may stop the honest operator, but the emulator must never turn one into a wrong hash, a wrong proof, or a directory that O2 guarantees but that later loads as a different state'; R9, 'The content hash must equal the root of the actual contents. This applies to every cached, incremental, or persisted hash ... and every snapshot the emulator itself writes', where 'Every snapshot the emulator itself writes means a directory that O2 guarantees'; section 5, 'A defect ... that damages a directory while O2 guarantees it, is not excused'. Same class as R1-O2-3 and R3-VARDIRTY-1 (host fault turned into a wrong hash).
5 Low only under the alternative reading of step 1.
candidates.claimed_severity: Critical (preferred: host fault turned into a wrong hash on a directory that meets O2's definition, R9 and section 4) / Low or Out of scope (if syncing again after a failed sync counts as the operator reusing a directory it had to discard)
candidates.threat_to_goal: Completeness failure. After the next reboot or cache eviction the honest operator loads its own synced directory and reads a root hash that is not the root of its contents (or runs from contents that lost pages while the cached tree still shows the old root). Its claims and proofs then differ from the state transition function, so a dishonest claim can win. Nothing warns the operator: the sync succeeded, and before the cache is dropped every check (cached root, rebuilt root) still passes.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r5/INVSTORE/syncretry.sh (root; tmpfs + loop + XFS with reflink=1, bare-metal template). The loop backing file is fully allocated, the template is cloned and synced, fstrim turns the free blocks into holes of the backing file and a filler file fills the tmpfs, so new blocks cannot be written (a full thin-provisioned disk). Then: load with SHARING_ALL, write 2048 RAM pages, get_root_hash (expected e15f3d65...), destroy, sync_stored -> 'unable to sync file machine/000000007ff00000-100000.dht: fsync() failed: No space left on device'. Remove the filler, sync_stored again -> SUCCESS. Before a remount the cached and rebuilt roots both equal the expected one. After umount/mount: cached root after reload 9a790f63... (wrong), root rebuilt with clear_hash_tree e15f3d65... (the contents), exit 1. Reproduced twice with the same result. On ext4 (same setup) the first failure aborts the journal and the second sync fails with EROFS. Kernel 6.18 has no device-mapper, so dm-error injection of EIO on overwrites was not possible.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.sh as /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r5/INVSTORE/syncretry.sh: build the full-backing XFS loop mount, make sync_stored fail once with ENOSPC, free the space, call sync_stored again, remount, and compare the root hash of a plain load with the hash recorded before destroy. Required: either the second sync_stored (and any later load of that directory) fails, or the reloaded root equals the recorded one (exit 0); today the second sync succeeds and the root differs (exit 1). Exit 2 when tmpfs, loop or mkfs.xfs are unavailable. A weaker, portable variant uses an LD_PRELOAD fsync shim that fails once with EIO and asserts that a later sync_stored of the same directory does not report success.

candidates.title: Stored revert mode: the documented crash-recovery rule resumes from a partially removed machine.revert and tells the operator to discard the only synced copies
candidates.component: cartesi-machine CLI --revert-mode=stored (src/cartesi-machine.lua revert_stored commit and remove_backup, help text) and the manual's 'Rolling Cartesi Machines directly from storage' sections with their Lua example; machine::remove_stored underneath
candidates.role: Support (CLI and manual example standing in for the honest operator's restart). The stored-machine API they drive is Honest operator.
candidates.location: src/cartesi-machine.lua 163-175 (help: 'after a crash or kill, resume from <directory>.revert if it exists'), 3893-3919 (commit: remove_stored(old backup) then rename of the synced clone), 3933-3939 (remove_backup at clean exit), 4924-4931; doc/README.md 2522-2540 and 5536-5576; src/machine.cpp machine::remove_stored 661-710 (files unlinked one by one in sorted order, config.json last, then rmdir)
candidates.description: A commit destroys the machine, syncs machine, clones it to machine.revert.tmp, syncs the clone, removes the old machine.revert with remove_stored, and renames the clone to machine.revert. The manual and the CLI help give the recovery rule by names: 'If machine.revert exists, it holds that state, so discard machine and machine.revert.tmp and clone machine.revert back to machine.' remove_stored is not atomic: it unlinks about 27 files one at a time and removes the directory last, so the name machine.revert stays on disk during the whole removal while the directory is already incomplete. A kill, crash or power loss in that window (in every commit after the first, and again at the clean exit, which 'syncs machine and then removes machine.revert') leaves: machine (synced, the committed state), machine.revert.tmp (synced, the same state) and a partial machine.revert. The rule sends the operator to the partial directory and tells it to discard the two guaranteed ones. The statement 'machine.revert therefore always holds a synced copy of the last committed state' and 'the names left on disk tell where the last committed state is' are false for this window. The CLI's own comment has the right invariant ('While <directory>.revert.tmp exists, the synced machine directory holds the committed state'), but the published rule checks machine.revert first. At the clean-exit removal no name distinguishes the case from a crash in the middle of an input.
candidates.trigger: A stop of the operator's process (kill, crash, power loss) while remove_stored(machine.revert) runs. No other party is involved; the guest and input senders only decide how often commits happen (one per accepted input).
candidates.reachability: Reached by following the manual: stored revert mode of cartesi-machine and the manual's Lua driver (run-rolling-calculator-from-storage.lua). Every accepted input performs the removal, so the window recurs for the whole epoch. The PRT stored player is not affected (prt.lua revert_interrupted_input picks by a content rehash and removes leftovers with REMOVE_FORCED).
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: the list excludes 'Defects that need the honest operator to reload a stored directory that O2 does not guarantee, such as one being written or shared when its process stopped'. Here the operator reloads such a directory only because the shipped manual and CLI help tell it to, and section 5 says 'O1 and O2 bind the emulator too. The tools and reference implementations that ship with it must follow them, and the emulator must make them possible to follow.' So the exclusion does not cover it (the reading that confirmed R1-O2-1). Under the literal reading it is Out of scope.

2 Role: 'No production deployment runs the player, the bridge or the CLI' (AUDIT.md): Support. Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator or a tool that computes claims'.

3 High and Medium cases: 'A persistence operation that fails loudly, without a wrong hash or damage to a directory that O2 guarantees, in an uncommon host setup that the manual documents, or while cleaning up after a stop' fits the clone of the partial directory (it fails loudly, no wrong hash). Also 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right': if the manual were right, the operator could always 'restart from a directory that O2 guarantees' (R4); in the stood-in honest role that R4 failure is Critical, capped at Medium for support.
4 Critical: not claimed (support component, loud failure).
5 Low if the manual's recovery text is read as informal advice rather than the reference procedure.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (preferred: support stand-in for an honest-operator R4/O2 failure, and the listed 'fails loudly ... while cleaning up after a stop' case) / Out of scope (literal O2 reload exclusion) / Low (recovery text read as informal)
candidates.threat_to_goal: R4 requires that 'After a stop, it restarts from a directory that O2 guarantees and keeps defending its claim.' An operator or script that applies the documented rule deletes machine and machine.revert.tmp, the only synced copies of the last committed state, and is left with a directory that cannot be cloned or loaded. It must then start the epoch over from the template and replay every input while the dispute clocks run. No wrong hash results.
candidates.evidence: With the real CLI: cartesi-machine --revert-mode=stored --load=machine,clone:<bare-metal template>,sharing:all --cmio-advance-state=input_file_index_begin:0,input_file_index_end:2,..., run under an LD_PRELOAD shim (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r5/INVSTORE/killunlink.c) that SIGKILLs the process before its 3rd unlink under machine.revert/. Left on disk: machine, machine.revert (25 of 27 files) and machine.revert.tmp. Applying the rule: clone_stored('machine.revert', ...) fails with 'unable to clone file from machine.revert/0000000000000000-8000.bin ...: open() failed: No such file or directory', while machine and machine.revert.tmp both load and rebuild to the same root (428a6bb8...). The same result with the API sequence of the manual's Lua example (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r5/INVSTORE/recover.lua).
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.sh: build the kill shim, run the CLI in stored revert mode over two inputs with KILL_UNLINK_MATCH=machine.revert/ and KILL_UNLINK_NTH=3, then apply the documented rule mechanically: if machine.revert exists, clone_stored(machine.revert, recovered) must succeed and its rebuilt root hash must equal the last committed state (the root printed before the interrupted commit, also held by machine.revert.tmp). Exit 1 while the clone fails; exit 0 once the name machine.revert never designates an incomplete directory (for example an atomic rename away before removal) or the rule is corrected.

candidates.title: cartesi-machine --store (and --create outside stored revert mode) never syncs the directory it writes, and has no option to do so: a template made the documented way is never a directory that O2 guarantees
candidates.component: cartesi-machine CLI (src/cartesi-machine.lua store_machine and the exit path), manual sections that create templates with --store
candidates.role: Support (CLI). It stands in for the honest operator obtaining its valid template.
candidates.location: src/cartesi-machine.lua store_machine 3734-3741 (machine:store only), exit path 4921-4939 (sync_stored only for the --load sync key or --revert-mode=stored), help for --store 961-972 (no sync key) and for sync 951-959; doc/README.md 1061-1070, 1388-1399, 2405, 4082-4100 (store presented as persistent, sync mentioned only for sharing at 1170-1179); src/cm.h 597-600 ('The stored files are durable only after cm_sync_stored() succeeds')
candidates.description: machine::store writes every backing file with ftruncate plus page-wise pwrite and never calls fsync; the C API states that the files are durable only after cm_sync_stored. The CLI's --store calls machine:store and exits. It offers a sync key only for --load with sharing, and syncs a --create directory only in stored revert mode. The manual builds every template with --store (for example --store=rolling-calculator-template) and describes the result as a persistent machine, mentioning the page cache only for shared loads. So the directory an operator produces as its template is never 'synced after the last change to its contents' and is not guaranteed by O2, and the CLI gives no way to make it so (only the Lua or C API, or loading it again with sharing:all,sync, which modifies it). After a power loss within the writeback window the files keep their full sizes (ftruncate is journaled) but data pages not yet flushed read as zeros; with large images the flusher writes small later files (hash-tree files, config.json) while big data files are only partly written, so the directory can load with a cached root equal to the intended hash over different contents. The operator produced this template itself, so O1 asks for no rebuild.
candidates.trigger: The operator's own template creation with the documented command, followed by a power loss or host crash before the kernel has written the files back (tens of seconds by default, longer for large machines). No other party is needed.
candidates.reachability: Honest operator's path item 'Obtaining its valid template', through the CLI. The PRT stored player clones the template and syncs its clone before use (prt.lua 2747-2776), which also flushes the source data on reflink and hard-link filesystems, so it is exposed only until that clone. An operator that loads the --store directory directly is exposed for as long as the directory is never synced.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: 'Defects that need the honest operator to reload a stored directory that O2 does not guarantee' would exclude it literally, since the directory is never synced. But section 5 says 'O1 and O2 bind the emulator too. The tools and reference implementations that ship with it must follow them, and the emulator must make them possible to follow', and the tool that produces templates neither syncs nor offers a way to. The host-fault entry excludes power loss only 'as long as the emulator does not turn them into a wrong hash'. R3-VARO2PLAYER-2 (missing parent-directory fsync in crisium, needing a filesystem without ordered metadata) was dropped; this site needs no special filesystem.
2 Role: CLI, Support ('No production deployment runs the player, the bridge or the CLI'), standing in for the honest operator.

3 High and Medium cases: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'. In the honest role, a tool on the operator's path that leaves its template outside O2 and can end in a cached root that is not the root of the contents (R9) would be Critical.
4 Critical: not claimed for a support component.
5 Low if the missing sync is read as a documentation gap of a tool.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (preferred: support tool not following O2 on the template it produces) / Out of scope (literal reading: an unsynced directory is not guaranteed, so reloading it is the operator's violation) / Low (documentation gap)
candidates.threat_to_goal: The template is the root of everything the honest operator defends. If a power loss corrupts an unsynced template and the operator keeps using it, its cached root still equals the on-chain commitment while its contents differ, so every later claim is wrong (completeness failure). Even without the fault, O2 as written cannot be followed with the documented commands.
candidates.evidence: strace -f -e trace=fsync,fdatasync,sync,syncfs of cartesi-machine --ram-image=<guest> --ram-length=64Mi --no-root-flash-drive --max-mcycle=0 --store=<dir>: 0 calls, 27 files written. The same trace of --load=<dir>,sharing:all,sync --revert-mode=none: 29 fsync calls. The power-loss outcome is reasoned, not run (no device-mapper in this kernel for dm-log-writes).
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.sh: run cartesi-machine --store=<dir> on a loop-mounted filesystem whose backing file is on tmpfs, and immediately after the command exits copy the backing file (what a power loss would leave), mount the copy and require that <dir> loads and that its root rebuilt with clear_hash_tree equals the hash printed by --final-hash. Simpler deterministic variant: trace the command and require an fsync of every stored file, of the directory and of its parent (exit 1 while there are none).

not_covered: Windows and macOS variants of os-filesystem.cpp and os-mapped-memory.cpp (clonefile, F_FULLFSYNC, FlushFileBuffers, the non-mmap fallback, read-only attribute handling) and hosts with pages larger than 16 KiB: read only in passing, nothing run.

JSON-RPC server and client paths of store, load, clone_stored, sync_stored, rename_stored and remove_stored (remote directories, client timeouts on long stores, fork_server children that inherit LOCK_SH descriptors of a non-shared machine). Only the fork refusal for shared machines was read.

Real power-loss injection: the kernel here has no device-mapper (no dm-log-writes, dm-flakey or dm-error). Candidate 3's outcome is reasoned plus a syscall trace; EIO on overwrites of allocated blocks (ext4 without journal abort) was not injected.

Reflink filesystems other than XFS. FICLONE errors other than ENOTSUP and EXDEV are rethrown by os::clone_file instead of falling back to a copy (btrfs flag mismatches, XFS with DAX, ZFS block cloning of a source with unsynced data). Not tested; probably a loud failure on an undocumented host.

flock semantics on NFS, 9p, FUSE and overlayfs (locks are the only guard between a shared machine and clone, sync or a second load); remove_stored and rename_stored take no lock at all and work on a directory a machine still maps (trusted-caller misuse, not pursued).

The PRT stored player after an injected sync failure: by reading, revert_interrupted_input keeps the epoch machine when a content rehash matches and later syncs succeed (the path candidate 1 relies on); not run. clone_loaded_directory clones an unsynced source; with the copy fallback a writeback error on the source is never observed by anyone. Reasoned only.

cartesi-machine stored mode error handling: a commit that fails after remove_stored(old backup) runs the close handler's revert, which removes machine; a rename failure can leave no copy at all. Needs a host fault, reasoned only.

Creating a machine directly in a directory writes config.json first (store and clone write it last): a kill between the PMA initialization and the DTB initialization leaves a directory that loads as a different machine. Excluded by O2 (stop during an API call) and the window is tiny; not reported.
config.json parsing (json-util.cpp) and the page-hash-tree-cache metadata checks were not fuzzed under the sanitizer build; hostile unhashed config fields belong to the R1-O1-2 family.

Hash-tree internals under allocation failure (R3-VARDIRTY-1 family), including a private page cache with borrowed entries that store() writes with the initialized tag, which would make the stored directory unloadable. Needs bad_alloc inside an update; not tested.
replace_memory_range and store with SHARING_NONE or SHARING_CONFIG (known R3-VARCACHE-1 and R2-DFSTORED-1) were not re-tested.

Checked without finding a defect: store, clone_stored, sync_stored, rename_stored, remove_stored and their partial-failure cleanup (scope_remove, scope_fail); create_file and copy_file sparse writes and SEEK_DATA; hard-link, reflink and copy selection and the shared-write guards (read-only mode, link count); mapped_memory lengths and partial pages; dirty-page-tree and page-cache initialization tags; load-time checks against guest-reachable states. A differential fuzz (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r5/INVSTORE/fuzz.lua: random advance, run, run_uarch, reset_uarch, log_step_uarch, log_reset_uarch, collect_*, write_memory, clear_hash_tree, get_proof on a SHARING_ALL machine with random destroy/sync/reload, store and clone) found cached root equal to rebuilt root in 9 bare-metal and 8 Linux runs on ext4 (copy fallback); cloning an unsynced source also matched.
